answer: Before the oven fires, the fireman logs its heat at every quarter hour and signs the page beside the batch it dried. A shale firing claimed as logged fails the book: the heat must have climbed to the firing mark at the inlet of the oven, and a batch never fired still smells of green leaf. Faking a week of oven logs means bribing the fireman, forging sixty readings and paying 8,600, and the vine page in the book is checked at every inspection, so tea whose firing was never logged is kept off the market.
